report.what_i_would_change: Print both boiling temperatures and the winning psig value on the whichBoilsMost line (the note promises it), make the assumption line name the refrigerant I actually entered instead of 'defaulting to R-410A', say which input was refused, and refuse above each gas's critical pressure (218 F for R-134a at 600 psig is nonsense).
report.notes: I got what I needed: 10 psig boils harder than 20 on every gas I tried (410A -42.4 F vs -28.0 F, 404A -30.7 vs -16.4, 22 -20.2 vs -5.1, 134a 6.7 vs 22.2), and its 40 F spots at 118 psig on 410A, 68.5 on 22 and 35 on 134a match my chart. The headline only says 'first pressure' with no temperatures even though its own note says it shows both, so I needed two more calls for the numbers, and it keeps saying it defaulted to R-410A even when I typed in 404A or 22 (the numbers show it really used my gas). It refused -20 psig, 1500 psig, gas code 9 and a typo'd pressure, though with one catch-all message that doesn't say which input was bad, and it let 600 psig on 134a through and answered 218 F, past the critical point, so I would not trust it at the far top end.

report.what_i_would_change: Flag or refuse impossible and absurd results (-58 psi, 106 psi, a barometer typed as 29.92 or 1013) and name the failing input in every refusal; print 'subcooling assumed 0 F, upper bound' on the answer line as its own note promises; make the assumption and purge advice follow the refrigerant chosen (it says ammonia on R-134a); allow liquid above 120 F for hot-site chillers; and add a purge limit plus a trend/log so it can actually track.
report.notes: For one reading it gave me the right number: 6.4, 7.5, 9.2, 2.3 and 6.3 psi all agreed with my P/T chart to about a tenth, and Denver's 12.2 psia versus sea level moved the answer exactly the 2.5 psi it should. But I asked for a tracker and this is a one-shot calculator with no trend, no purge limit and no log, and it printed -58.0, 106.2, 21.6 (barometer typed as 29.92) and 1004.7 psi (1013 mbar) as plain answers, showed blank subcooling as a bare '0 F' with no 'upper bound' on the answer line, and refused with the same generic list of limits instead of naming the bad input. The R-134a answers still say the refrigerant is ammonia and carry ammonia purge advice, and it refused my 128 F liquid on a hot-roof chiller, so I would use it as a careful spot check on an ammonia plant, not as the tracker.

report.notes: For 15 psig at sea level it gave -23.5 F dew (-25.0 F bubble), but the breakdown stops at the gauge-to-absolute step (29.7 psia), so the 29.7-psia-to-temperature part is a black box, and typing just 15 got refused with no hint that elevation and basis were missing. The published R404A PT table I checked online has 15 psig at about -21.5 F dew and -22.6 F bubble, so this reads about 2 F cold at 15 psig and 5 to 9 F hot at 237 to 312 psig, which is too far off to hang superheat or subcooling on. The refusals (-20 psig, 700 psig, bad basis) work but list all three ranges instead of naming the bad one, and the 5280 ft correction goes the right way (27.1 psia, -27.4 F), but the canned assumption text keeps saying sea level, dew point and 15 psig no matter what I typed.

report.what_i_would_change: Warn or refuse on impossible results (it printed -32.1 F superheat without a word), name the input behind a refusal, and recheck the R-404A column (59.5 F against the 56 F on my gauge).
report.notes: It was right to refuse to guess the refrigerant and to show what my 32 psig and 55.9 F reads on each one (410A 70.3, 404A 59.5, 22 46.5, 134a 18.9), and on a 410A house job and an R-22 check it matched my chart, but I only got a superheat to compare, not an answer: the 266 psig, the 105.7 line and the 2.8 goal were never used, so no subcooling and no word on what 56 against 2.8 means. I don't trust its 404A column yet, since 59.5 doesn't match the 56 on my gauge and it puts 404A at about 36 F at 85 psig where my chart says nearer 40, and its stock assumption text is off too (it says 32 psig is about 17 F on R-22 when its own R-22 answer works out to about 9 F). Worst for the field, it printed -32.1 F superheat without a word when I put my head pressure in the suction slot, and every refusal is the same two-reason text, so it said the refrigerant wasn't confirmed when I'd entered R-22 and my pressure was the problem, and said to re-read my gauge when my readings were fine.
